title: vault() and vault_list() functions fail silently — no _last_error, inconsistent with the other two Vault scripting surfaces
existing_state: The three ways to read Vault from a script disagree on error surfacing. The vault: step fails the step (or sets _last_error with on_error: continue); inline {{vault:path#key}} sets _last_error and resolves to empty string on every failure path (Services/Scripting/ScriptContext.cs:711, 722, 742, 753); but the vault(path, key) and vault_list(prefix) functions catch VaultException and return null while setting nothing (Services/Scripting/Functions/VaultFunctions.cs:38-41 and :65-68), and also return null for config problems like a missing profile (:31-32, :58-59). A script using functions in expressions cannot distinguish 'secret has no such key' from 'Vault is sealed/unreachable' from 'no profile configured' — all are an undifferentiated null.
recommendation: In both catch blocks (and the no-profile early returns), set context's _last_error with the VaultException message, matching ResolveVaultExpression's contract — a two-line change per site in VaultFunctions.cs. Document the convention (null + _last_error) in the function reference so script authors can branch on it: if(vault(...) == null) { print(_last_error) }.
user_benefit: Script authors get one consistent error contract across all three Vault surfaces, making vault-dependent scripts debuggable instead of failing with bare nulls.
